subject: Evaluation success criteria + commercial terms for on‑prem deployment
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro call — on‑prem evaluation plan

Thanks for the call this morning, Soojin — good context.

Priya and I sketched out the evaluation window and a few commercial questions that matter to Procurement here before we move to a pilot agreement: 
- Success criteria: throughput (>250 rps sustained for 4‑hour windows), tail latency p95 < 250ms on our typical 8k token prompts, and deterministic KV cache behavior when we checkpoint models.
- Licensing question: for a private/on‑prem topology we need clarity on platform fee vs. per‑token runtime fee. Procurement will want a milestone‑based pricing schedule (trial -> pilot -> production) with clear commit thresholds.
- Discounts & credits: are discounts available for an initial commit (12–18 months)? Would Redwood consider waiving the platform fee for the first quarter of production if we meet an agreed ramp?

Can you put together a proposed MAP that maps evaluation milestones to commercial triggers (pricing/commits/discounts) and a draft timeline so we can share internally? Also send any standard On‑Prem Terms appendix — legal will want to start a redline.

Thanks,
Liam
Sr. Dir, Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Singh <priya@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation success criteria + commercial terms for on‑prem deployment

Liam — thanks, this is exactly the right framing. I attached an initial MAP (Acme_MAP_v2.pdf) and a short commercial summary below. I've also looped in Marissa (AE) and Aditya (Contracts) so we can align on timing and legal asks.

Summary (high level):
- 4‑week evaluation (POC) — no platform fee, Redwood provides limited on‑prem support (remote onboarding, 2 tune sessions). Success gates: throughput and p95 targets + a short quality check on 200 prompts.
- 8‑week pilot — production‑like capacity, 25% discounted runtime pricing; platform fee optional (we propose reduced platform fee if commit to production within 60 days).
- Production ramp (committed) — 12‑month initial commitment with tiered unit pricing tied to sustained monthly token/embedding volumes. Platform fee applies; proposal below outlines tiered rollback caps and a partial platform‑fee waiver schedule tied to ramp milestones.

Commercial asks we can accommodate:
1) Platform fee waiver: waive first full month of platform fee if customer executes production commit within 45 days of pilot completion.
2) Discounting: up to 20% off runtime rates on a 12‑month committed spend (bands tied to volume).
3) Escalation & audit: include a 30‑day audit window and SOC2 sn‑list confirmation in the appendix.

I'll add concrete numbers in the MAP doc. If that high‑level is acceptable we'll push the On‑Prem Appendix (Redwood_OnPrem_Terms_Appendix.docx) and a DocuSign skeleton.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_MAP_v2.pdf (MAP v2, milestones + timelines)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation success criteria + commercial terms for on‑prem deployment

Liam — quick note on commercial structure from the AE side. Long story short: we can shape pricing around the MAP milestones but need a firm committed spend to lock the deepest discounts. Proposed approach:
- POC: Redwood covers engineering support; no platform fee.
- Pilot (metered): 25% off runtime for up to 90 days, platform fee set at 50% of standard rate during pilot if they don't sign commit within 60 days of pilot end.
- Production commit: 12‑month minimum; tiered runtime discounts (10/15/20% at 3 bands); platform fee returns to standard but we will offer a 50% credit of the first month if ramp milestones are met.

Two commercial caveats:
- We need an explicit ramp schedule in the MAP to protect Redwood from underutilization risk.
- Any platform‑level SLA exceptions (e.g., custom regional adjacency) should be scoped as an additional professional services line item.

I'll prepare suggested numbers and a short table for the MAP PDF by EOD tomorrow.

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation success criteria + commercial terms for on‑prem deployment

Looping in legal confirmation items so Procurement can run a parallel review. From Redwood legal: 
- We'll provide the On‑Prem Terms Appendix (attached) with the platform fee schedule and standard indemnities.
- Requested change: limit the platform‑fee waiver to a single calendar month and require the customer to sign the commitment addendum with the redlines agreed BEFORE the waiver is applied.
- Timing: legal can do a first round redline within 3 business days of receiving ACME's comments.

Liam / Priya — please can you flag any non‑standard clauses your procurement team requires (export controls, data residency attestations, HSM/KMS specifics)? That will speed the redline.

Aditya
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Singh <priya@acme-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation success criteria + commercial terms for on‑prem deployment

All — thank you. Procurement reviewed the MAP and had two asks: 
1) Make the platform fee waiver conditional on hitting a defined 30‑day average token consumption (we proposed 60M tokens) during the pilot, rather than the 45‑day time window.
2) Push for a 90‑day right to early termination during pilot if production KPIs are not met (with a partial credit for consumed runtime).

On the legal side, export controls are a non‑issue; we do require a commitment in the appendix around audit log retention for 12 months and an SOC2 attestation copy.

If Redwood can accept the consumption‑based waiver trigger (60M tokens during pilot) and agree on the term around early termination with a defined credit back, we can sign the commitment addendum shortly after your redlines.

Thanks,
Priya
Dir, Software Infrastructure
Acme Analytics

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@acme-analytics.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation success criteria + commercial terms for on‑prem deployment

Priya — appreciate the clear asks. We can accept the consumption‑based waiver (60M tokens during pilot) as an alternative to the 45‑day clock, and we'll include a 90‑day early termination right for the pilot with a prorated runtime credit (calculation in the MAP appendix).

Next steps:
- Finalize MAP PDF with the consumption metric and termination credit language (attached).
- Legal to push the On‑Prem Appendix redline (Redwood_OnPrem_Terms_Appendix.docx) — Aditya to circulate by Monday.
- DocuSign skeleton (link below) will include the commitment addendum and the appendix so you can route to Procurement for signature once redlines are completed.

Signing link: https://docusign.com/embeddedSigning?token=abc123-acme
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-acme-eval

If these are green, Marissa and I will schedule a short 30‑minute alignment to walk the MAP and next steps.

Best,
Soojin
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
